prompt: Bug report from a user: "My GPS app writes the `# units: ft` line at the end of the file, after the points. trailhead then reports a highest point of 14115 m for a hike that tops out at 14,115 ft (about 4302 m). The file is attached as `pikes-peak.csv`." Find the cause and fix it.
bash_commands:
python - <<'EOF'
p="src/trailhead/track.py"
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("points.append(_parse_point(line, number, scale))","points.append(_parse_point(line, number))")
s=s.replace("    return Track(name, points)\n","    # Units may be declared after the points, so scale only once the file is read.\n    if scale != 1.0:\n        points = [Point(p.lat, p.lon, p.ele * scale) for p in points]\n    return Track(name, points)\n")
s=s.replace("def _parse_point(line: str, number: int, scale: float)","def _parse_point(line: str, number: int)")
s=s.replace("Point(lat, lon, ele * scale)\n\n\ndef load","Point(lat, lon, ele)\n\n\ndef load")
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
cat >> tests/test_track.py <<'EOF'


def test_units_line_after_points_still_applies():
    text = "lat,lon,ele\n0,0,1000\n0,0.01,2000\n# units: ft\n"
    track = parse_track(text)
    assert [p.ele for p in track.points] == [pytest.approx(304.8), pytest.approx(609.6)]
EOF
head -12 tests/test_track.py | grep -n import; python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; python -m trailhead summary pikes-peak.csv
PYTHONPATH=src python -m trailhead summary pikes-peak.csv; git diff --stat
